audit.title: Get a Random Number (Chainlink VRF v2.5)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections open with orientation prose ("For this example, create a new subscription…") rather than a liftable canonical answer. The intro states the guide's purpose clearly, but no section leads with a self-contained one-sentence answer to "how do I request randomness in VRF v2.5." Weak on standalone chunkability.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good — 7 headings, 1 H1, zero level skips, logical lifecycle flow. Weakness: 0 tables; the request-parameter definitions (`keyHash`, `callbackGasLimit`, etc.) and the LINK-vs-native cost comparison both beg for tables an engine can extract as rows.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 37 prose numerals, real costs, gas figures (20,000/word, 100,000 default), confirmations (3), addresses, version pins (v2.5, v1.3.0, ^0.8.20). Best-in-class here.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 26 links, 5 to primary sources (GitHub contract source at pinned tag, Remix). No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Parameter definitions are crisp and near first use ("`bytes32 keyHash`: The gas lane key hash value…"). Missing: a one-sentence canonical definition of Chainlink VRF v2.5 itself near the top for the "what is" query.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — measured facts show 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read, but the deterministic scan found none.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — single complete contract, tagged `sol`, real imports, hardcoded Sepolia coordinator and keyHash, SPDX header. The unassigned-identifier flags (SPDX, THIS, EXAMPLE…) are disclaimer comments, not real gaps. No expected-output shown, minor.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers full lifecycle including cleanup — good. Gap: no troubleshooting/FAQ section and no symptom-phrased headings (e.g. "callback never returned," "request stuck pending," "callbackGasLimit too low"). The answers exist inline but aren't retrievable by symptom.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong and consistent ("VRF v2.5," "subscription," "consuming contract"). Minor vague quantifiers ("a few minutes," "several random values").

audit.summary: This is a solid, concrete VRF v2.5 tutorial: it walks setup → deploy → request → cleanup with real cost figures (7 LINK to fund, ~0.06 LINK actual), a complete copy-pasteable Solidity contract, and inline links to primary sources (Remix, GitHub). Its biggest GEO strength is code completeness and specifics; its biggest opportunity is machine-readability metadata (no JSON-LD, missing canonical, no dates) combined with the absence of symptom/error-phrased sections that would win troubleshooting retrieval. The honest verdict: strong content that gives engines good material to quote, but under-instrumented for parsing and under-covered for the "why did my request fail" queries devs actually type.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema + canonical + last-updated
recommendations.issue: measured facts: "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, and a self-referential `canonical` URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parseability and trust; a canonical URL is required for the harness to score `hit_expected_source`.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: answers to failures are buried inline ("If your `callbackGasLimit` is not sufficient, the callback will fail")
recommendations.change: add "## Troubleshooting VRF requests" with H3s phrased as queries: "Why is my VRF request stuck pending?", "Callback failed / fulfillRandomWords not called", "request not found error", each leading with the fix.
recommendations.why: devs and agents query by symptom; concept-titled prose loses retrieval that question-phrased headings win, even with the answer present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Lead each major section with a liftable canonical sentence
recommendations.where: "Request random values" and "Create and deploy a VRF compatible contract"
recommendations.issue: sections open with "For this example…" / procedural framing
recommendations.change: prepend one self-contained sentence, e.g. "To request randomness in VRF v2.5, call `requestRandomWords(bool enableNativePayment)` on your consumer contract; VRF returns values via the `fulfillRandomWords()` callback."
recommendations.why: a crisp first sentence survives chunking and is quoted verbatim; procedural openers don't stand alone in RAG.

recommendations.title: Convert request parameters to a table
recommendations.issue: measured facts: "0 table(s)"; params are a prose bullet list
recommendations.change: render a table with columns Parameter | Type | Example value | Purpose (e.g. `callbackGasLimit` | `uint32` | `100_000` | gas for the callback).
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract per-parameter reasons and default values as discrete rows.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical definition + native-vs-LINK comparison table
recommendations.where: intro paragraph and step 5 of "Create and fund a subscription"
recommendations.issue: no one-line definition of VRF v2.5; payment costs given as parenthetical prose
recommendations.change: open with "Chainlink VRF v2.5 is a verifiable random number generator that lets smart contracts access provably fair randomness via a funded subscription." Add a small table: Payment | Fund with | Approx. actual cost (LINK | 7 LINK | ~0.06 LINK; ETH | 0.03 ETH | ~0.000247 ETH).
recommendations.why: a verbatim definition wins "what is" queries; the cost table makes the highest-value specifics extractable.

recommendations.title: Show expected output / return shape for read functions
recommendations.issue: no example of what these calls return
recommendations.change: add a short example return, e.g. `getRequestStatus(requestId) → (fulfilled: true, randomWords: [12…, 98…])`.
recommendations.why: concrete expected output helps agents verify task completion and raises snippet trust.

antiPatterns: Minor vague quantifiers: "a few minutes," "several random values," "many" — acceptable in a tutorial but could be tightened where a number exists.
Two "(Image: …)" placeholders in place of rendered screenshots — no alt-bearing content for engines; consider a one-line text description of what the step shows.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — clean.
offPageNotes: Site-level: `llms.txt` is already referenced at top — good; ensure this URL is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Metadata absence may be a rendering artifact — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so JSON-LD/canonical/og tags can be verified rather than assumed missing.
Freshness cadence: adding and maintaining a visible `dateModified` is a site-template change, not just this page.
